Duration ratio 0.6189 TIC (0.51 Gaia) with FLAME/ GSP-Phot radius ~0.44 vs TIC 0.36 - improved Gaia astrometry / spectroscopy would refine stellar density and planet size.

dossier.public_summary: A 0.63-day 485 ppm dip recurs 205 times on the M dwarf, centres on the target in difference images and shows no secondary or odd-even change, with a size of about 0.89-1.08 Earth radii. Despite heavy spot variability and one noisy sector, the depth is steady across sectors and the rotation period is unrelated. The best explanation is a small planet, pending ground-based follow-up to remove spot systematics and confirm duration.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target and >3 sigma from any neighbour that could fake it with <=25% eclipse, ruling out a blended neighbour EB despite 1 plausible_within_1px star.

reasons.why: Planet-sized (<2 R_E) for an M dwarf (Teff 3351 K rad 0.3597) even with larger Gaia radius.
No odd-even difference, no secondary (snr 2.124 <5) and shape not V-like, disfavouring EB at twice period with different primary/secondary depths.
Depth is consistent sector-to-sector (p 0.6655, top 3 share 0.238, 205 transits, SNR 15.1), as expected for a uniform transit aperture on the target, not a variable spot or few bad events.
